intro: Short answers to the questions people usually ask before opening Studio or reading the documentation.

items.summary: Why LGS1920? What does it mean?
items.body: LGS1920 stands for La Grande Sure, a 1,920-metre summit in the Chartreuse massif, in the French Alps, at GPS coordinates 45°20′07″ N, 5°42′11″ E (45.3353, 5.7031).
items.bodyAfter: It is a mountain that means a great deal to me: it is part of my family roots, and I was barely twelve when I climbed it for the first time with my family. At the time, it was my Mont Blanc — better still, my Everest.
items.bodyFinal: One of Studio’s journey samples is, appropriately, named LGS1920. It is one of my favourite hikes, and I still hike it once a year, 54 years later.

items.summary: Why can’t I load a file from the Downloads folder on my mobile or tablet?
items.body: On Android and iOS, files in the dedicated Downloads directory cannot be read directly by a browser.
items.bodyAfter: LGS1920 follows a privacy-first approach: your files remain on your device and are read locally by the browser. To work around this restriction, we would have to send the file contents unencrypted to our backend so it could download the file on your behalf. We refuse to do that.

items.body: Working data stays in the browser by default. Cesium Ion is only needed for Cesium-backed data.
